body.statement: Let a three-way tensor have a decomposition into \(R\) nonzero rank-one terms with factor matrices of Kruskal ranks \(k_1,k_2,k_3\). If \(k_1+k_2+k_3\ge 2R+2\), then the tensor rank is \(R\) and the decomposition is unique up to a common permutation of the terms and reciprocal nonzero scalings within each term.

source.verbatim_statement: Suppose rank(A) + rank(B) + rank(C) is at least 2R + 2. Then there exist diagonal matrices and a common permutation matrix.

attestation.note: Verified from the source-of-record Elsevier article page for DOI 10.1016/0024-3795(77)90069-6, whose abstract explicitly reproduces Theorem 4a and the factor-equivalence conclusion, on 2026-09-05.
